He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale Bulldogs]] and the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. At Yale in 2024, he earned first-team All-[[Ivy League]] honors, the [[2024 Ivy League men's basketball tournament|Ivy League tournament]] [[most valuable player|MVP]], and led the league in rebounds and blocks per game. At Michigan in 2025, he was a second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] selection, leading the conference in rebounds per game and double-doubles. He competed for [[Israel men's national under-20 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[2023 FIBA U20 European Championship]], winning a [[silver medal]] and earning all-tournament team honors. Wolf was selected 27th overall by the Nets in the first round of the [[2025 NBA draft]]. ==Early and personal life== Wolf was born in [[Glencoe, Illinois]], in the United States, and is Jewish.{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/us-israeli-basketball-star-danny-wolf-seeks-glory-in-march-madness-and-likely-the-nba/|title=US-Israeli basketball star Danny Wolf seeks glory in March Madness — and likely the NBA |author=Jacob Gurvis| website=Times of Israel}}{{Cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/danny-wolf/19240|title=Danny Wolf – 2023–24 – Men's Basketball|website=Yale University}} His oldest brother, Josh, played basketball at [[Lehigh University]], and his other older brother, Jake, played basketball at [[Washington University in St. Louis]]. His father Joe (who played high school basketball) is {{convert|6|ft|8|in|m|2|abbr=on}}, his mother Tina (who played high school tennis) is {{convert|5|ft|10|in|m|2|abbr=on}}, and each of his two brothers are {{convert|6|ft|10|in|m|2|abbr=on}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/draft/2025/05/07/danny-wolf-nba-draft-scouting-report-and-intel/83491031007/|title=Danny Wolf: NBA draft scouting report and intel |date=May 7, 2025|website=USA Today|author= Cyro Asseo de Choch}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/columnists/mitch-albom/2025/03/09/danny-wolf-michigan-jewish/82056047007//|title=Mitch Albom: Danny Wolf is a rare breed — proud Jewish 7-foot star who plays like a guard |website=Detroit Free Press}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/07/09/after-a-series-of-growth-spurts-lake-forest-academys-danny-wolf-hits-6-10-and-starts-receiving-division-i-offers-on-the-first-day-it-was-the-coolest-thing-ever/|title=After a series of growth spurts, Lake Forest Academy's Danny Wolf hits 6-10 and starts receiving Division I offers on the first day: 'It was the coolest thing ever.'|first=Bobby |last=Narang|date=July 9, 2020|work=The Chicago Tribune}} Danny is 7 feet (2.13 m) tall and weighs 250 pounds (113 kg). He studied at a [[Solomon Schechter Day School Association|Solomon Schechter]] [[Jewish day school]] until fifth grade, keeps [[kosher]], and celebrated his ''[[bar mitzvah]]'' at the [[Western Wall]] in Jerusalem, Israel. ==High school career== Wolf attended [[Lake Forest Academy]] in Illinois for three years, where at the start of his freshman season he was 6-foot-3 and played on the varsity basketball team.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/02/the-lone-wolf-how-michigans-7-foot-guard-became-college-basketballs-most-unique-player.html|title=The lone Wolf: How Michigan's 7-foot guard became college basketball's most unique player |date=February 26, 2025|author=Andrew Kahn|website=mlive}} He then transferred to [[Northfield Mount Hermon School]] in [[Massachusetts]] for his senior year, where he helped the team reach the finals in both the NEPSAC Triple-A championship and the national prep championship. Under his leadership, the team was ranked number 11 in the country for the majority of the season. Additionally, he received a [[McDonald's All-American Game]] nomination, and was a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/minnesota/Article/Minnesota-Basketball-Recruiting-Danny-Wolf-Ben-Johnson-166669458/|title=2022 PF Danny Wolf discusses his Minnesota official visit|website=247Sports|author=Ryan James|date=June 17, 2021}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/11/12/recruiting-notes-6-foot-10-junior-danny-wolf-cites-uncertainty-in-illinois-opportunity-on-east-coast-in-decision-to-transfer-from-lake-forest-academy/|title=Recruiting notes: 6-foot-10 junior Danny Wolf cites uncertainty in Illinois, opportunity on East Coast in decision to transfer from Lake Forest Academy|author=Bobby Narang |work=Chicago Tribune|date=November 12, 2020}}{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/college-prospect-spotlight-yales-danny-wolf-#:~:text=Notable%20Accolades,experience%20at%20the%20college%20level|title=College Prospect Spotlight: Yale's Danny Wolf; This week, we highlight the spectacular play of Yale center Danny Wolf|date=December 21, 2023|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=February 21, 2024}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] because of the elite combination of academics and basketball that the school provided.{{cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/danny-wolf/19240|title=Men's Basketball Roster – Danny Wolf|last=|date=October 27, 2023|website=[[Yale]]|access-date=February 21, 2024}} ==College career== ===Yale=== In his freshman season at [[Yale University]], 2022–23, Wolf primarily played for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Bulldogs]] as a backup to forwards [[EJ Jarvis]], Isaiah Kelly, and Matt Knowling, averaging 2.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 0.4 blocks. After the season, he received Yale's John C. Cobb Award, which is given to the team's rookie of the year. At the start of his sophomore season, 2023–24, Wolf moved into a starting role and became the focal point of the Bulldogs’ offense.{{Cite web|url=https://bvmsports.com/2024/01/03/yale-vs-howard-sophomore-sensation-danny-wolf-leads-bulldogs-as-6-point-favorites-in-college-basketball-showdown/|title=Yale vs. Howard: Sophomore sensation Danny Wolf leads Bulldogs as 6-point favorites in college basketball showdown|date=January 3, 2024|website=BVM Sports}}{{Cite web|url=https://ivyleague.com/news/2024/1/22/mens-basketball-wolf-mack-repeat-ivy-mens-hoops-weekly-winners.aspx|title=Wolf, Mack Repeat as Ivy Men's Hoops Weekly Award Winners|date=January 22, 2024|website=ivyleague.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2024/02/15/dom-amore-danny-wolf-weirdly-unbelievable-adds-new-dimension-to-yales-basketball-aspirations/|author=Dom Amor|title= Danny Wolf, 'weirdly unbelievable,' adds new dimension to Yale's basketball aspirations|date=February 15, 2024|work=Harford Courant}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.ctinsider.com/college/article/danny-wolf-yale-mens-basketball-ivy-league-18641768.php|title=Danny Wolf powers Yale basketball team to six-game winning streak|work=CT Insider|date=February 1, 2024|first=Myer|last=Lee}} On November 19, 2023, he posted then-career-highs of 21 points, 11 rebounds, and four assists in an overtime win over [[Gardner-Webb University]]. Wolf's play earned him the Ivy League Player of the Week five times, including three straight from January 23, 2024, to February 12.{{Cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2024/2/12/mens-basketball-wolf-earns-ivy-player-of-week-honors-for-fifth-time.aspx|title=Wolf Earns Ivy Player of Week Honors for Fifth Time|date=February 12, 2024|website=Yale University}}{{cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2024/2/12/mens-basketball-wolf-earns-ivy-player-of-week-honors-for-fifth-time.aspx#:~:text=Wolf%2C%20who%20scored%2025%20points,awards%20in%20a%20single%20season|title=Wolf Earns Ivy Player of Week Honors for Fifth Time|last=Bennett|first=Tim|date=February 12, 2024|website=Yale Athletics|access-date=February 21, 2024}} During that stretch, he averaged 17.6 points, 10.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists, and 0.8 blocks, leading the Bulldogs to an undefeated record during the span. Wolf became just the seventh player in Ivy League history to earn five Player of the Week awards in a single season. In 2023–24, Wolf led the [[Ivy League]] with 310 rebounds, 247 defensive rebounds, 9.7 rebounds per game, and 1.3 blocks per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/danny-wolf-1.html|title=Danny Wolf College Stats|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} He finished the year averaging 14.1 points per game (10th in the league), with 43 blocks (second), 63 offensive rebounds (third), 176 field goals (third), a .472 field goal percentage (fourth), and 33 steals (tenth). He earned unanimous first team All-Ivy honors, a [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] District 13 first-team selection, was named the most outstanding player in the [[Ivy League men's basketball tournament|Ivy League tournament]], and was named [[Academic All-District]].{{Cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2024/3/20/mens-basketball-wolf-jones-finalists-for-collegeinsider-awards.aspx|title=Wolf, Jones Finalists for CollegeInsider Awards|date=March 20, 2024|website=Yale University}}{{Cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2024/3/26/mens-basketball-wolf-townsend-named-academic-all-district.aspx|title=Wolf, Townsend Named Academic All-District |date=March 26, 2024|website=Yale Bulldogs}} ===Michigan=== On April 20, 2024, Wolf transferred to the [[University of Michigan]] to play for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Wolverines]] in the [[Big Ten Conference]].{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2024/04/20/danny-wolf-transfer-portal-michigan-basketball-yale-dusty-may-commitment-height/73398502007/|title=7-foot Yale transfer Danny Wolf commits to Dusty May, Michigan basketball|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|first=Craig|last=Meyer|date=April 20, 2024|access-date=April 22, 2024}} On November 4, 2024, in his first game with Michigan, against [[2024–25 Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball team|Cleveland State]], Wolf led all players with 19 points and 13 rebounds, while adding three blocks, three steals, and two assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401707875/cleveland-st-michigan|title=Michigan v. Cleveland State (November 4, 2024)|website=[[ESPN.com]]}} In the seventh game of the season, against [[2024–25 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]], he had his third [[double-double]] of the season, leading all players with 20 points and 14 rebounds as Michigan became the [[Fort Myers Tip-Off]] champions.{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/11/27/michigan-basketball-takes-down-no-22-xavier-to-win-fort-myers-tip-off-title/76619810007/|title=Michigan basketball routs No. 22 Xavier to win Fort Myers Tip-Off title|work=[[The Detroit News]]}} In the next game, against [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]], Wolf scored 20 points, grabbed a team-high seven rebounds, and recorded a game-high five assists, three steals, and five blocked shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/12/03/michigan-basketball-stuns-wisconsin-67-64-despite-frigid-1st-half/76752779007/|title= 7-footers lift Michigan basketball after brutal start to 67-64 upset of No. 11 Wisconsin|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=December 3, 2024}} On January 4, 2025, against [[2024–25 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]], he had 21 points, 13 rebounds, seven assists, and a career-high six blocks, earning his seventh double-double of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=401721330 |title=Michigan v.
